label: A binary is probed by spawning '<path> --version' with a 3000 ms timeout (spawnSync sync, execFile async); stdout and stderr are joined with a newline and parsed together.

parseOpencodeVersion trims, splits lines then whitespace, and tests each token and adjacent token pair against VERSION_PATTERN, whose optional leading word lets 'opencode v2.0.32' match; group 1 is the major and the first match wins.
Major 1 maps to 'unsupported', major 2 to 'v2', every other parseable major and every unparseable or missing version to 'unknown'; SUPPORTED_FAMILIES is the frozen list ['v2'].

evaluate consumes the family: an explicit options.version wins, otherwise it auto-resolves with resolveOpencodeVersionSync when the command matches an opencode run shape and at least one rule declares appliesTo; rules without appliesTo default to SUPPORTED_FAMILIES.

For v2 only rules whose appliesTo includes v2 run; for unsupported and unknown every rule runs, and a rule not covering all supported families is downgraded to warn, while a rule covering v2 keeps its declared severity so error rules still block.

The engine never rewrites the command; it only rewrites a declared severity down to warn for unresolved narrower rules and substitutes the DSH patch message, returning violation objects for the adapters to deny or advise on.
Resolved families live in an in-process Map keyed by JSON [realpath, size, mtimeMs], so a replaced binary misses the cache; clearOpencodeVersionCache empties it.

Overrides are OPENCODE_BIN plus PATH: bare names resolve on PATH, literal $OPENCODE_BIN or ${OPENCODE_BIN} tokens are replaced by the env value, and a path-qualified binary is probed only when its canonical identity matches a trusted executable.

Resolver errors degrade to 'unknown': async timeout, throw or empty output is uncached; a successful probe yielding an unparseable version is cached as unknown; the sync resolver catches everything and returns unknown, caching its parse result.
A version family alone never refuses a dispatch; only a rule whose effective severity is block or error does.
